title: Put the close-fitting lid on a packed board-game box with both hands, seating all four sides without wedging
instruction: Put the lid squarely onto the packed game box so it seats all the way down over the base without spilling the contents or moving the box off its marks.
context: The lid is wider than one gripper in both directions, a few degrees of tilt jams its skirts on the base's rim, and only a level, square lower with both arms seats it. Anyone who has tidied away a board game, jigsaw puzzle, or shoebox has seen a wide two-piece lid catch cocked half-on. Here the packed base and matching telescoping lid of a named game box span 33.5 by 23.1 cm against a parallel gripper's 9.4 cm opening, and the lid's four 5.3 cm skirts clear the base walls by an estimated 1.5 mm per side, so a lid tilted past about 2.8 degrees catches on the rim. One hand cannot span the lid from above, shoving it sideways knocks the base off its marks without lifting the skirt over the rim, and fingers placed under the lip get trapped against the base wall. Both arms must press inward on opposite outer short walls, carry the lid level, align all four corners and lower it smoothly home; done carelessly the lid ends up resting on the box cocked, a corner standing proud.
setup: Station bench; cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x away from the arms, y left. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. One fixed layout; nothing varies by seed. Game box: Ravensburger Junior Labyrinth, article 20847; the maker's page (ravensburger.de/de-DE/produkte/spiele/kinderspiele/junior-labyrinth-20847) gives 'Schachtelgröße: 5,50 x 33,50 x 23,10 cm', the closed box (lid outside 33.5 x 23.1 x 5.5 cm); every other figure is an estimate derived from it (see fidelity and README). Base: open top up, 328.4 x 224.4 x 52.0 mm outside, 1.8 mm wall, 175 g empty, centered at (43.5, 0.0) cm (+/- 1.0 mm, yaw +/- 0.5 deg), long axis along y, framed by four yellow matte tape corner L-marks (30 x 30 mm, 4.5 mm outside the base walls so 1.2 mm stays visible outside the seated lid). Inside the base: the game's own contents, which the real trial uses (maker's list: 1 board, 4 pawns, 17 maze cards, 12 chips; about 320 g, estimate), packed below the rim. The simulation stands three rigid blocks of that total mass in for them: tile stack (70 x 70 x 24 mm, 160 g), token deck (58 x 86 x 18 mm, 126 g), and pawn (24 mm diameter x 34 mm tall, 34 g), resting >= 15 mm below the rim (packed base 495 g). Lid: matching top lid, 331.4 x 227.4 x 53.2 mm inside (1.5 mm play per side; 335.0 x 231.0 x 55.0 mm outside, 185 g), resting top-up with open skirt down at (18.5, 0.0) cm (+/- 1.0 mm, yaw +/- 0.5 deg, 22.3 mm clear of the base). Checked against the tape marks and a top-camera photo.
scoring: Read when the trial ends; the episode ends early once 1.0 has held for 3.5 s. Whole-trial faults (checked from the trial video; final photo, ruler, and caliper confirm the end state): 0.0 for the rest of the trial if at any moment the base tilts > 15.0 degrees from horizontal, any of its four outer corners shifts > 25.0 mm horizontally from its start position, or any game piece leaves the base's interior (in the simulation, any of the three stand-in blocks). Otherwise 1.0 when, continuously for 1.0 s (20 steps), the lid is seated -- roof height only: every one of its four roof corners lies within 1.0 mm of the closed height calipered on this box with the lid pressed fully home (first minutes, step 1; 55.0 mm in the simulator), lid tilt <= 2.0 degrees, and the lid sits over the box (no centring test: the walls bound it) -- with all free bodies at rest (< 10 mm/s, < 0.10 rad/s), both grippers' grasp points >= 30.0 mm from lid and base, and the box on its marks. 0.5 when the lid instead rests on the box but is not seated: continuously for 1.0 s all free bodies are at rest, both grippers >= 30.0 mm clear, the lid is over the box and pressing on it (at least 0.5 N of lid-to-box contact; no straddle requirement -- a lid cocked with one skirt inside the base is the everyday half result), lid tilt <= 15.0 degrees, and the seated geometry above fails. 0.0 otherwise (idle, lid off the box or lying on the bench, moving, hands not clear, or any whole-trial fault). Real-trial reading (ruler): 1.0 'every corner within 1 mm of the calipered closed height, lid level'; 0.5 'the lid rests on the box but a corner stands more than 1 mm proud'.
reset_notes: Lift the lid straight off with both hands; check that the game's contents (board, pawns, maze cards, chips) lie inside the base below the rim; align the base at (43.5, 0.0) cm (+/- 1.0 mm, yaw +/- 0.5 deg) inside its four 4.5 mm yellow corner tape marks and set the lid top-up at (18.5, 0.0) cm (+/- 1.0 mm, yaw +/- 0.5 deg); verify against a top-camera photo. Reset takes about 15 seconds; nothing is consumed, sharp, sticky, or wet.
fidelity: Five-wall hollow rigid greyboard base and lid (0.4 mm contact offset) plus three rigid stand-in blocks for the game's contents (320 g, estimate) in PhysX at 240 Hz; zero welds, hidden joints, or computed pushes. Lid outside 33.5 x 23.1 x 5.5 cm is the maker's figure (article 20847); walls, per-side clearance, masses, and frictions are estimates derived from it (README table). Not modelled: the contents' shapes, cardboard wall flex under squeeze, trapped-air cushioning, and printed artwork text.
